questions.reasoning: 247 CMR 8.01(16) states flatly: 'A registered pharmacist preceptor shall not directly supervise more than two pharmacy interns at one time.' This is a standalone cap on the preceptor-to-intern relationship and is independent of the pharmacist-to-support-personnel ratio in 247 CMR 8.06(3). Being under the overall support-personnel ratio therefore does not authorise a third intern. A is wrong because the 8.06(3) ratio is not the only applicable limit; B and C invent hour and task carve-outs that 8.01(16) does not contain; D is wrong because nothing limits precepting to teaching hospitals.

247 CMR 8.01(15) provides: 'A pharmacy intern acting under the direct supervision of a registered pharmacy preceptor may supervise pharmacy technicians.' The stem states the intern is under direct preceptor supervision, so the condition is met. A contradicts 8.01(15); B inverts the rule, since the preceptor's presence is the precondition and not its absence; C invents an hours threshold; E invents a setting restriction.

247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)1 permits one pharmacist for a maximum of four support personnel only if (a) at least one of the four is a certified pharmacy technician and one is a pharmacy intern; or (b) at least two are certified pharmacy technicians; or (c) two are pharmacy interns. Option A (one CPhT plus one intern plus two technicians) satisfies clause (a). Option B (two CPhTs plus two trainees) satisfies clause (b). Option C has one intern and no CPhT, so it fails (a), (b) and (c). Option D has neither a CPhT nor an intern. Option E has only one CPhT and no intern. 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)2 (maximum three support personnel with at least one intern or CPhT) is unavailable because the pharmacist wants four.

247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) excludes 'Sales clerks, messengers, delivery personnel, secretaries and any other persons who do not fall within the definitions of a pharmacy intern, certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy technician trainee ... for purposes of determining the ratios set forth in 247 CMR 8.06(3) as long as such persons are not supporting the pharmacist in any professional capacity.' A front-store cashier who never assists with prescriptions meets both limbs, so the cashier is not counted. B is wrong on the plain text; C invents a documented-exemption condition; D invents an hours-based condition; E invents fractional counting.

247 CMR 8.04(3) sets out exactly three consequences when a certified pharmacy technician's certification lapses: the technician (a) is 'limited to performing the duties and responsibilities of a pharmacy technician, as set forth in 247 CMR 8.02'; (b) shall 'use the title "pharmacy technician"'; and (c) shall 'be counted as a "pharmacy technician" in calculating supervisory ratios, as set forth in 247 CMR 8.06(3).' Those are options A, B and C. D is wrong because the individual retains a current Board technician licence under 247 CMR 8.02(1) and may continue working as a pharmacy technician. E is wrong because 247 CMR 8.04(3) contains no automatic suspension of the Board licence; lapse of a private certifying body's certification is not Board discipline.

247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) permits a certified pharmacy technician, 'after identifying him or herself as such,' to 'request refill authorizations from the prescriber or prescriber's agent and, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty, receive new or omitted prescription information from the prescriber or agent, except where otherwise prohibited by federal or state laws and regulations.' Directions omitted from a written prescription already on file are 'omitted prescription information', so pharmacist-on-duty approval is the operative condition. A invents a schedule limitation; B is wrong because 247 CMR 8.04(4)(e) bars a CPhT from final patient dispensing process validation; C contradicts the express permission; E is wrong because the pharmacist's approval is required.

247 CMR 8.04(4)(d) permits a certified pharmacy technician, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty, to 'perform prescription transfers between pharmacies for prescriptions issued for controlled substances in Schedule VI only.' In Massachusetts, M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 3 places in Schedule VI any prescription drug not included in Schedules I through V, so Schedule VI is the correct and exhaustive statement of the permitted class. A ignores the Schedule VI limit; B wrongly extends to Schedules III through V; D contradicts the express permission; E is wrong because Schedule V is excluded and 'non-controlled prescription' is not the operative Massachusetts category.

247 CMR 8.02(6)(c) allows a pharmacy technician, with the approval of the pharmacist on duty, to 'request and accept authorizations for refills from a prescriber or a prescriber's agent provided that no information has changed from the previous prescription.' An increase in the daily dose is a change from the previous prescription, so the proviso fails and the technician may not accept it. Pre-approval of the call (A) does not cure the change; a read-back (B) is not a regulatory cure; C is wrong because 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) bars a technician from contacting prescribers concerning therapy modification and later pharmacist verification does not retroactively authorise the technician's act; D is wrong because even a certified pharmacy technician is confined under 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) to refill authorisations plus new or omitted information and is barred by 8.04(4)(e) from therapy modification.

247 CMR 8.03(4)(c) provides without qualification that 'A pharmacy technician trainee may not take prescriptions over the telephone.' 247 CMR 8.03(4)(b) permits a trainee to perform pharmacy technician duties under direct pharmacist supervision only 'Except as set forth in 247 CMR 8.03(4)(c)', so direct supervision (A), a second handset (B), the drug's schedule (C) and accrued hours (E) are all irrelevant to the prohibition.

247 CMR 8.03(5) provides that an individual 'may not work as a pharmacy technician trainee for more than 1500 hours or for more than one year, whichever period is shorter, unless: (a) the Board grants an extension; (b) the individual has not yet reached 18 years of age; or (c) the individual has not yet completed at least 500 hours of employment as a pharmacy technician trainee', and further that an individual who has worked beyond those limits before turning 18 'shall submit an application for a pharmacy technician license within 30 days of his or her 18th birthday.' A restates the limit, B is the express Board-extension exception, C is the express under-18 exception, and E is the express 30-day post-18th-birthday application duty. D is fabricated; short staffing appears nowhere in 247 CMR 8.03(5).

The applicant already satisfies 247 CMR 8.02(3)(a) through (d) (age 18 or older, high school diploma, good moral character, no drug-related felony). The remaining requirement is 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e), satisfied by any one of: '1. hold certification conferred by a board approved certifying body'; '2. hold a license as a pharmacy technician in another state provided that the requirements for licensure in the original state are substantially equivalent to the requirements of the Board and the license is in good standing at the time of the application'; or '3. achieve a Board-approved passing score on a Board-approved pharmacy technician assessment examination after having successfully completed' a Board-approved training program or a minimum of 500 hours of trainee employment. A, B and C map onto 8.02(3)(e)1, 2 and 3.a respectively. D and E are not listed pathways.

247 CMR 8.07(1) makes a pharmacy technician licence expire every two years on the licensee's birthdate, and 247 CMR 8.07(2) provides that the licence 'must be timely renewed to continue practice' and that 'Any practice as a pharmacy technician after the expiration date of a pharmacy technician license shall constitute unlicensed practice as a pharmacy technician subjecting the individual to any and all penalties established for unlicensed practice.' The six worked shifts were therefore unlicensed practice. 247 CMR 8.07(3) permits renewal on payment of back and late fees but does not retroactively legitimise the intervening practice, so A fails; no grace period exists, so B fails; pharmacist supervision does not substitute for licensure, so C fails; and the violation exists independently of whether the Board investigates, so D fails.

247 CMR 8.05(1) provides that 'Accountability for and security of Schedule II controlled substances shall be the direct responsibility of the pharmacist' (A). 247 CMR 8.05(2)(a) permits a pharmacy technician, under pharmacist supervision, to 'assist in the transporting of Schedule II controlled substances' (B), and 8.05(2)(b) permits a certified pharmacy technician to 'assist in the transporting and handling of Schedule II controlled substances' (C). The closing proviso of 8.05(2) requires that the pharmacist has approved the individual to assist 'as evidenced by written policies and procedures to be followed in the pharmacy' (D). E is false: 247 CMR 8.05(3) provides that a certified pharmacy technician, pharmacy technician, or pharmacy technician trainee 'may not handle any hydrocodone-only extended release medication that is not in an abuse deterrent form', and supervision does not lift that bar.

247 CMR 8.01(18) requires that 'A pharmacy intern shall provide written notification to the Board within 14 days of his or her withdrawal from an approved College/School of Pharmacy or PharmD program.' The duty is the intern's own, is triggered by the withdrawal itself, and is not deferred by an intention to reapply. A is wrong because 247 CMR 8.01(2)(b) requires current PharmD enrolment for intern eligibility; C states the wrong period; D misassigns the duty to the preceptor; E invents a one-year condition.

247 CMR 8.01(8) provides that a PharmD graduate from an approved College/School of Pharmacy who has accepted a residency in Massachusetts 'shall apply for and obtain a pharmacy intern license until such time as he or she obtains a Massachusetts pharmacist license', and that such a graduate 'shall: (a) hold a Massachusetts pharmacist license; or (b) hold Massachusetts pharmacy intern license and be supervised by a pharmacist.' Because she has not yet passed NAPLEX or MPJE she cannot satisfy limb (a), since 247 CMR 3.01(4) requires passage of both examinations, so limb (b) is the arrangement that satisfies the regulation. A and B are wrong because a residency appointment and a degree confer no independent practice authority; C is wrong because limb (b) expressly permits the intern-licence route; E is wrong because reciprocity under 247 CMR 3.02 requires prior licensure by examination elsewhere.

247 CMR 8.01(7) provides that 'Before the commencement of a pharmacy internship in Massachusetts, a graduate of a non-approved college/school of pharmacy must have authorization, issued within the preceding year, from NABP to sit for the FPGEE and must provide a copy of the NABP FPGEE authorization to the Board, along with any other documentation required by the Board.' An authorization issued twenty months ago was not issued within the preceding year, so a current authorization must be obtained and supplied to the Board. A is wrong because the currency requirement is express; B is wrong because FPGEC certification does not displace the internship requirement (247 CMR 3.01(2)(d)); D and E impose requirements the regulation does not.

247 CMR 8.01(1)(a) requires 'at least 1500 hours of Board-approved pharmacy internship experience, of which: 1. at least 1000 hours has been acquired in a pharmacy or pharmacy-related setting approved by the Board; and 2. at least 500 hours has been acquired in any one, or any combination of Board-approved internships(s) in the following areas: a. clinical pharmacy; b. demonstration project; c. manufacturing; d. analytical or industrial pharmacy' (A and B). 247 CMR 8.01(1)(b) supplies the alternative pathway of 'at least 1500 intern hours acquired through experiential pharmacy education, provided the student is a graduate of an ACPE accredited college or university' (C). 247 CMR 8.01(11) permits the Board to grant credit for out-of-state internship experience where an affidavit or certificate of approval from the jurisdiction where it was acquired is presented (D). E is false: 247 CMR 8.01(5) provides that internship hours 'may be acquired throughout a calendar year' and imposes no single-calendar-year completion rule; the only temporal cap is the 12-hours-per-day credit limit in 247 CMR 8.01(4).

247 CMR 8.04(3)(b) requires that on lapse of certification the individual 'use the title "pharmacy technician"', and 247 CMR 8.02(6)(a) requires that 'A pharmacy technician shall wear a name tag which indicates the individual's first name and the title "Pharmacy Technician."' The tag must therefore be changed to read Pharmacy Technician. B and E would continue an inaccurate title contrary to 8.04(3)(b); C would leave the individual with no name tag, contrary to the mandatory tag requirement in 8.02(6)(a); D is wrong because the individual still holds a valid Board pharmacy technician licence and is not a trainee under 247 CMR 8.03.

247 CMR 8.06(1) provides that the pharmacist Manager of Record or the Director of Pharmacy 'shall make the following available to the Board upon request: (a) a list of currently employed certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacy technician trainees; (b) a written description of the duties delegated to certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacy technician trainees; and (c) a written description of the scopes of responsibility for certified pharmacy technicians, pharmacy technicians, and pharmacy technician trainees.' The obligation is production on request, not advance filing, so A is wrong. The duty is not limited by practice setting (B), is not limited to certified pharmacy technicians (C), and is not conditioned on the use of on-the-job training (E); 247 CMR 8.06(2) separately requires on-the-job training guidelines to be provided to the Board on request.

247 CMR 3.01(1)(c) requires an ACPE-accredited graduate to have 'completed a pharmacy internship in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01(1)', and 247 CMR 3.01(2)(d) imposes the identical internship requirement on a graduate of a non-approved college/school of pharmacy (A). 247 CMR 3.01(2)(b) requires the foreign graduate to have 'received official Foreign Pharmacy Graduate Examination Committee (FPGEC) Certification from NABP', with 3.01(2)(c) requiring submission of the certificate and official NABP notification (B). 247 CMR 3.01(1)(a) and 3.01(2)(a) each require the applicant to be '18 years of age or older by the scheduled date of the examination applied for' (C). D is false because 3.01(2)(d) retains the internship requirement alongside FPGEC certification. E is false because 3.01(1)(d) requires good moral character of the ACPE graduate.

247 CMR 3.01(7) provides that 'An applicant who fails either NAPLEX or MPJE must reapply to sit for the examination which the applicant failed within one year of the administration date of the original examination in order for both examination scores to be considered together. If the applicant does not pass both NAPLEX and MPJE within this one year period, the applicant must apply to retake both NAPLEX and MPJE.' Applying fourteen months after the original MPJE administration date falls outside the one-year window, so the passing NAPLEX score can no longer be paired with an MPJE result and both examinations must be retaken. A is therefore wrong; B, C and E invent consequences the regulation does not provide.

247 CMR 3.02(1)(a) provides that 'Whenever an applicant has been notified by NABP that the applicant does not meet the requirements for licensure by reciprocity, the applicant may in writing request the Board to review the basis of NABP's decision', and 3.02(1)(b) confirms that 'The Board shall make the final determination of any applicant's eligibility to be registered as a pharmacist by reciprocity.' NABP acts only as the Board's agent for the preliminary evaluation, so A is wrong. B, C and E are not the avenue the regulation supplies.

The opening paragraph of 247 CMR 3.02 conditions reciprocity on proof that the applicant 'has been licensed by examination in another state or jurisdiction and that the applicant is in good standing in all states where the applicant holds a license' (A). 247 CMR 3.02(2)(a)3 and 3.02(3)(a)3 each require a 'passing score (at least 75%) on MPJE' (B); 3.02(2)(a)2 and 3.02(3)(a)2 each require 'documentation of internship experience in accordance with 247 CMR 8.01' (C); and 3.02(2)(a)4 and 3.02(3)(a)4 each provide that 'if requested, the applicant shall personally appear before the Board to discuss any matter related to the application' (D). E is false because the MPJE is expressly required on the reciprocity pathway.

247 CMR 3.04(1) states that 'A retired status is a nondisciplinary status' (A). 247 CMR 3.04(3) states that 'A licensee with a retired status may not practice' (B). 247 CMR 3.04(2)(a) conditions eligibility on having 'a license that is not surrendered, suspended or revoked at the time of the petition' (C). D is false because 247 CMR 3.04(4) expressly preserves the Board's power to initiate, pursue or take disciplinary action against a licensee whose licence is in retired status, including changing the status to revoked or suspended. E is false because the second sentence of 247 CMR 3.04(1) provides that 'The Board may decline to review any petition for reinstatement or return to current status', so review is discretionary rather than mandatory.

247 CMR 3.05 provides that 'No person shall be denied initial licensure or denied renewal due to any complaint, criminal charge, conviction, judgment, discipline, or other sanction due to providing or assisting in providing, or dispensing medication for, reproductive health care services or gender-affirming health care services, as defined at M.G.L. c. 12, s. 11I 1/2, so long as the services provided would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with standards for good professional practice in Massachusetts.' The stem supplies both conditions, so renewal may not be denied on the basis of that sanction. A is contrary to 3.05; B, C and E would each condition or defer renewal on the protected sanction, which 3.05 forbids.

247 CMR 4.02(5) provides that 'An applicant for personal registration renewal who has failed to renew his or her personal registration for more than two years, and whose personal registration has not been suspended or revoked by the Board, shall take and pass the Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Examination and meet all other conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal.' A lapse of about 30 months exceeds two years and the registration was never suspended or revoked, so 4.02(5) governs. A is insufficient because fees alone satisfy only 247 CMR 4.02(2); B is insufficient because additional continuing education is the 60-day route in 4.02(4); C is wrong because NAPLEX is only a possible additional condition under 4.02(7) for registrations revoked or suspended for more than two years; E is not a renewal route.

A nine-month disciplinary suspension falls within 247 CMR 4.02(6), which governs a registration 'revoked or ... suspended for between six months and two years' and provides that the applicant 'shall take and pass the Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Examination and meet all conditions as determined by the Board as a prerequisite to registration renewal.' That yields A, B and D. C is false because the discretionary NAPLEX condition appears only in 247 CMR 4.02(7), which applies to registrations revoked or suspended for more than two years. E is false because 4.02(6) makes the MPJE and the Board's conditions prerequisites, so serving the suspension is not by itself sufficient.

247 CMR 4.03(4) requires a registrant to 'complete a minimum of 20 contact hours of continuing education each calendar year of the two-year renewal cycle', and 247 CMR 4.03(5) provides that 'Contact hours of continuing education may not be carried over from one calendar year to another.' Completing zero hours in the first calendar year therefore cannot be repaired by completing 40 hours in the second. A is wrong because hours are required in both years, not forbidden in the second; B is wrong because 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b) permits up to 15 home-study hours per calendar year, so home study is not barred outright (the 30 planned home-study hours would separately breach that cap); C is wrong because 247 CMR 4.00 sets no annual maximum, only the eight-contact-hours-per-calendar-day limit in 4.03(7); E is wrong because 4.03(4)(a) imposes no sequencing requirement on the two annual pharmacy law hours.

247 CMR 4.03(4)(c) requires 'at least five contact hours per calendar year of continuing education in the area of sterile compounding' of a registrant who 'oversees or is directly engaged in the practice of sterile compounding or who practices in a pharmacy licensed pursuant to M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39G or 39I'; she satisfies both limbs (A). 247 CMR 4.03(4)(e) requires a registrant who 'oversees or is engaged in the administration of vaccines' to complete 'at least one contact hour of continuing education on the topic of immunizations during the two-year renewal cycle' (B). 247 CMR 4.03(4)(a) provides that 'All registrants must complete at least two contact hours per calendar year in the area of pharmacy law', which applies to her as it does to every registrant (C). D is false because the three-hour complex non-sterile compounding overlay in 247 CMR 4.03(4)(d) is triggered by complex non-sterile compounding or a M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39H licence, neither of which the facts supply. E is false because 4.03(4)(c) states a single five-hour minimum and contains no doubling mechanism.

247 CMR 4.03(6) provides that 'in the event of extenuating circumstances an applicant for renewal of personal registration who has failed to complete the requisite number of contact hours of continuing education ... shall submit to the Board a detailed statement, signed under the penalties of perjury, setting forth with detail and specificity such extenuating circumstances. In such case, the Board shall determine whether or not a renewal shall be granted.' The regulation therefore directs a sworn detailed statement for Board determination. A is wrong because self-certification of a shortfall is not the prescribed route and 247 CMR 4.03(2) bars renewal without the requisite hours; B is wrong because 247 CMR 4.03(5) forbids carry-over and no cure period exists; D is wrong because retired status under 247 CMR 3.04(2)(b) requires an intent to retire permanently; E is wrong because the sworn statement must come from the applicant.

247 CMR 4.02(8) provides that 'Pursuant to M.G.L. c. 112, s. 1B(c), the personal registration of a registrant who is engaged in active service in the armed forces remains valid until 90 days following the release of the registrant from active duty. The continuing education requirement in 247 CMR 4.03 shall not apply to the biennial cycle immediately preceding December 31st of an even-numbered year if the registrant is engaged in active service after October 1st of that even-numbered year.' Entering active service in November of an even-numbered year is service after October 1st of that even-numbered year, so both limbs operate. M.G.L. c. 112, s. 1B(c) confirms that the licence 'shall remain valid until the licensee or certificate holder is released from active duty and for a period of not less than 90 days following that release.' A is wrong because the December 31 expiry in 4.02(1) is displaced; C overstates by making validity indefinite and treating continuing education as merely deferred; D wrongly retains the continuing education requirement; E invents a pre-deployment waiver.

247 CMR 4.06(1) requires a pharmacist to maintain documentation or statements of credit containing '(a) the name of the authorized provider; (b) the participants name; (c) the title and number of the continuing education program; (d) the date of completion of the program; and (e) the number of contact hours of continuing education earned.' Options A, B, C and D correspond to 4.06(1)(a), (c), (d) and (e). E is false because the registrant's employer is not among the enumerated elements. 247 CMR 4.06(2) requires the documentation to be provided to the Board on request and in response to random audits.

247 CMR 4.04(4) provides that 'A provider whose request for provider authorization or program approval is denied by the Executive Director, or the Executive Directors designee and who seeks further review of his of her request may appeal the decision to the full Board by a written petition submitted within 30 days of the notice of denial.' A is wrong because 247 CMR 4.04(2) requires each request to be 'submitted to the Board no less than 30 days in advance of the date of the proposed program's presentation', so a submission 20 days out was untimely and the denial may rest on that ground alone. C is wrong because 4.04(1) and 4.04(4) expressly make a designee's denial reviewable by the full Board. D is wrong because 4.04(4) is not limited to ACPE-accredited providers; 4.04(5) treats current ACPE or AMA CME Category 1 standing as a separate route to authorized-provider status. E states the wrong trigger date, since the 30 days run from the notice of denial.

attestation: I solved all 33 items only from the sanitized blind package and current official sources, and opened none of the sealed items before writing this lock.
